title: Select All Students
description: Write a query to retrieve all columns from the students table.
hints: Use SELECT * to get all columns
explanation: SELECT * retrieves all columns from the specified table. Use FROM to specify which table to query.

title: Select Student Names
description: Write a query to retrieve only the name column from the students table.
hints: Specify only the column you need after SELECT
explanation: Instead of *, list specific columns to retrieve only the data you need. This is more efficient than SELECT *.

title: Select Distinct Grades
description: Write a query to get all unique grade values from the students table.
explanation: DISTINCT removes duplicate values from the result set, showing each unique grade only once.

title: SELECT Clause Purpose
description: What does the SELECT clause do in SQL?
hints: Think about what data you get back
It works with FROM to specify the source
explanation: SELECT specifies which columns to retrieve from the database. It defines the output structure of your query.

title: Count Students
description: Write a query to count how many students are in the students table.
hints: Use COUNT(*) to count all rows
explanation: COUNT(*) returns the total number of rows in a table. It counts all rows including those with NULL values.

title: Select Students with Age
description: Write a query to get student names and their ages, sorted by age descending.
hints: Use ORDER BY with DESC for descending
solutionSql: SELECT name, age FROM students ORDER BY age DESC;
explanation: ORDER BY sorts the results. DESC means descending (highest first). Without DESC, sorting is ascending by default.

title: Top 3 Students by Age
description: Write a query to get the 3 oldest students from the students table.
hints: Use LIMIT 3 to get only the first 3
solutionSql: SELECT name, age FROM students ORDER BY age DESC LIMIT 3;
explanation: LIMIT restricts the number of rows returned. Combined with ORDER BY, it lets you get the top N records.

title: Table Alias Syntax
description: Which syntax correctly creates a table alias for 'students' as 's'?
hints: The alias comes after the table name
explanation: Table aliases shorten long table names and make queries more readable. The syntax is: table_name AS alias.

title: Concatenate Name Fields
description: Write a query that returns each student's full name as 'LastName, FirstName' format. Since our table only has one name column, just select name and grade together.
hints: Use comma to separate columns in SELECT
explanation: You can select multiple columns by separating them with commas. The order in SELECT determines the column order in the result.

title: Predict Query Output
description: What will this query return? SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT grade) FROM students;
hints: How many unique grades are there?
explanation: COUNT(DISTINCT grade) counts the number of unique grade values. In our data: Freshman, Sophomore, Senior = 3 unique grades.

title: List All Courses
description: Write a query to get all course titles from the courses table.
explanation: Simple SELECT on a single column returns all values in that column, one per row.

title: Students in Science Department
description: This query has an error. Fix it: SELECT name, age FORM students WHERE grade = 'Freshman';
solutionSql: SELECT name, age FROM students WHERE grade = 'Freshman';
explanation: SQL keywords must be spelled correctly. 'FORM' is not a valid SQL keyword; use 'FROM' instead.
brokenQuery: SELECT name, age FORM students WHERE grade = 'Freshman';

title: Get Teacher Subjects
description: Write a query to get the subject and department for each teacher.
explanation: Multiple columns are selected by listing them separated by commas after SELECT.

title: Fill in the SELECT Statement
description: Complete the query to get all student names: SELECT ___ FROM students;
explanation: The asterisk (*) is a wildcard that represents all columns in a table.

title: Enrollment Count per Student
description: Write a query to get each student's name and how many courses they are enrolled in.
solutionSql: SELECT s.name, COUNT(*) as enrollment_count FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON s.id = e.student_id GROUP BY s.name;
explanation: JOIN combines rows from two tables. COUNT(*) with GROUP BY gives the count per group. The alias 'as enrollment_count' names the result column.
